chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The ritual bath (ghusl) on the Day of Arafah is when the sun sets, and one combines the noon (Dhuhr) and afternoon (Asr) prayers with one Adhan and two Iqamas.' And he stops the Talbiyah when the sun sets. Narrated.

key_terms.بِأَذَانٍ وَإِقَامَتَيْنِ: With one Adhan and two Iqamas

ai.seo_question: What are the specific prayer and ritual bath rulings for the Day of Arafah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that the Ghusl for the Day of Arafah commences at sunset, marking the transition into the night of Arafah, which is crucial for the pilgrim's spiritual preparation before the stand at the plain. The hadith details the practical method of combining Dhuhr and Asr prayers using a single Adhan and two Iqamas, reflecting the specific jurisprudential view of the Ahl al-Bayt on prayer consolidation during Hajj. Furthermore, it establishes the precise moment for ceasing the Talbiyah, aligning the pilgrim's verbal devotion with the changing ritual status as the day concludes.
